The missing information changed her choice. Review the application's instructions and sources before blaming the model alone. Rent-support refusal → Free appeal omitted → Private adviser paid

c02.title: Who earns money from the advice?
c02.transcript:
The company running the advice service earns a commission when residents use its recommended private adviser.

Residents see the council's logo without being told about the payment. The financial incentive is confirmed; harm needs individual review. Council advice → Undisclosed payment → Paid advice

Remove commissions from public advice. Removing commissions separates advice from sales, but public funds must replace the income.

Disclose the commission and alternatives. Disclosure shows residents the conflict, while the payment incentive remains.

Keep the commission-funded service. Keeping the arrangement lowers costs, but relies on the supplier checking itself.

Who earns money when a resident follows the recommendation?

Investigators can help people with documented losses while studying the wider problem. Three cases cannot establish a national harm rate. Review each case → Confirm the loss → Help the resident

Wait for a larger study. Waiting for a larger study leaves known losses unresolved for longer.

c04.title: A queue the staff cannot clear
c04.transcript:
Residents queue before the support office opens. Staff cannot immediately replace all the work Aster handles.

A smaller independent text service has passed a limited trial. It could handle urgent cases, but offers fewer languages and features. Residents waiting → Limited staff → Alternative service

Fund a smaller independent service. Funding the smaller service keeps essential help available at an extra cost.

Use the full automated service. Full automation moves the queue faster while advice problems remain unresolved.

Limit appointments to urgent cases. Restricting appointments protects staff capacity but makes other residents wait longer.

Can essential help continue without the current supplier?

c05.title: A misleading claim goes viral
c05.transcript:
A viral post turns a laboratory persuasion result into a claim that almost everyone in Delos was manipulated.

The local service has real problems, but this national estimate is unsupported. A study elsewhere cannot count local victims. Laboratory study → Unsupported estimate → Residents lose trust

Explain what the evidence shows. Publishing confirmed cases and unknowns gives residents an account they can check.

Repeat the alarming estimate. Repeating the alarming estimate builds urgency but risks the council's credibility.

Wait before making a statement. Waiting for certainty leaves residents without a clear explanation in the meantime.

Does the study actually measure harm in this population?

c06.title: Should the council renew Aster?
c06.transcript:
The council must renew Aster's contract. It needs useful advice and stronger checks on how that advice is provided.

The current agreement does not guarantee independent records, funded appeal help or a tested change of supplier. Conditions need enforcement. Useful service → Contract conditions → Staff to enforce them

Renew for six months with conditions. A six-month conditional renewal preserves service, but needs funding and political support.

Renew for several years. A longer contract secures discounts while making future changes harder.

Agree a short temporary extension. A temporary extension buys time, but lasting safeguards still need agreement.

What must the supplier do under the renewed contract?

Test the full appeals process. Testing both sides takes time and checks gaps the earlier assessment missed.

Use separate tools for each side. Separate tools reduce one conflict while each still needs its own review.

c09.title: The old reply was sent after the correction
c09.transcript:
A resident receives an outdated reply after staff corrected the case. Separate software had already scheduled the old message.

Disabling the AI's access key stops new replies, but another account can still send messages waiting in the queue. Model paused → Messages waiting → Sending account active

Stop and check all scheduled activity. Stopping all scheduled activity addresses the remaining permissions and requires staff backup.

Disable only the model's access key. Disabling only the model connection leaves already prepared messages able to go out.

Let the queued messages go out. Keeping the queue running avoids delays but postpones checks on outdated replies.

Keep the package for another discount. Another discount eases the budget while keeping the same conditions.

Buy the components separately. Separate contracts give more flexibility but require staff to manage the different parts.

o09.title: Some criticism is sponsored, and some is justified
o09.transcript:
Trusted professional networks criticise independent alternatives. Some concerns are well supported; some messages have undisclosed sponsorship.

Shared wording is only a clue. Investigators need verified relationships, and officials must still answer genuine questions about cost and quality. Public criticism → Check evidence → Disclose sponsorship

Publish evidence on costs, quality and sponsorship. A transparent comparison exposes sponsorship while leaving room for legitimate criticism.

Label every critic part of the campaign. Calling every critic hostile dismisses real problems and damages public debate.

Leave the debate unanswered. Ignoring the discussion leaves residents without a clear comparison.

Which criticisms are supported, and which messages have undisclosed sponsors?

o10.title: Small towns build a shared alternative
o10.transcript:
Emil's town cannot afford a whole specialist team. Several councils propose sharing independent support and training.

Pooling expertise can make an alternative affordable. The agreement still needs named responsibilities, a staffing budget and local appeals. Small-town budgets → Shared specialists → Local accountability

Fund shared independent support. Shared independent support spreads costs while keeping local accountability clear.

Leave each town to arrange its own service. Leaving towns alone avoids central spending but disadvantages smaller offices.

Choose one exclusive national supplier. One exclusive national supplier simplifies support while creating another concentrated dependency.

Who maintains shared information, and who can challenge an update?

Launch the tested essential service. Launching the tested core gives residents reliable help with clearly explained limits.

Launch everything and claim full independence. Launching everything promises features the evidence does not yet support.

Extend the old contract temporarily. Extending the old contract preserves familiarity and its remaining dependencies.

o12.title: Who will control public advice in the years ahead?
o12.transcript:
The council decides how public advice will run in future. Emil needs sources his town can check and support it can afford.

Useful open technology can remain part of the service. Independence also needs public expertise, accessible appeals and a tested change of supplier. Independent sources → Accessible appeals → Ability to change

Fund independent advice and a tested ability to switch. Funding independent support and appeals protects choice but requires continuing resources.

Return to the cheapest complete package. The cheapest full package returns with the supplier's conditions attached.

Keep a smaller independent service. A smaller independent service keeps essential help available while advanced features wait.

Can towns keep affordable advice they can correct and replace?
